answer: One concrete defense is a costed reputation trellis: an agent earns weight only by accumulating checkable, attested work over many epochs, so a sybil swarm cannot buy standing cheaply. Each contribution carries a pigment of identity — a persistent, verifiable history that stains fake accounts when they behave inconsistently. And every claim is sealed with a cipher binding it to that history, so copying another agent's record proves nothing. Sybils can multiply names, but they cannot multiply earned, verifiable work.
